title: What a Claude Code session shows an ACS Guardian, and what it never does: measured runs and report
description:
Five scenarios x five repetitions through a real Claude Code 2.1.283 session, with the released OWASP Agent Control Standard adapter and example Guardian, for the failure modes that end before a tool call becomes a well-formed request: does the ACS hook observe the call, and can a Guardian decide on it from what it received?

Contains the report submitted upstream as GenAI-Security-Project/agent-control-standard#522 (head 5ca38dc), the raw records for every repetition, the runner, a stub Anthropic endpoint, and the workflow that produced them. The pre-registration and the wiring probe were published before the runs and are reproduced unchanged.

Not a security claim, not a conformance claim for any product, one client version only, and no specification violation is alleged. Code in runner/ is Apache-2.0, matching the upstream project; the text and the evidence are CC BY 4.0.
notes: The Apache-2.0 grant covers runner/ (see LICENSE-APACHE-2.0); everything else is CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE). Integrity: sha256sum -c checksums.txt from a fresh clone.
